original_question: For X, let L(F) be closure of a family F of subsets of X under lim inf, and say X has the delta-property if for each open omega-cover U of X, X is in L(U). Is this delta-property equivalent to the property Omega choose Gamma (equivalently S1(Omega,Gamma))?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Problem 5.1: Is the δ-property equivalent to the property that every open ω-cover contains a γ-subcover (equivalently, to S1(Ω,Γ))?
correct_elements: Your draft captures the right target almost exactly: it identifies the δ-property via lim inf closure, asks about equivalence with the Gerlits–Nagy γ-property, and correctly notes the paper’s explicit equivalence between the binomial property and S1(Ω,Γ).
missing_details: The paper’s ambient scope is sets of real numbers; your draft leaves X as an arbitrary space, which is broader than the chapter’s stated scope.
To be fully stand-alone, you should define lim inf explicitly: lim inf A_n = ⋃_{m∈N} ⋂_{n≥m} A_n.
You should specify that L(F) is the smallest family of subsets of X containing F and closed under the lim inf operation.
You should define an open ω-cover: a family U of open subsets of X such that X is not itself a member of U and every finite F ⊆ X is contained in some U ∈ U.
You should define a γ-cover: an infinite open cover V of X such that each x ∈ X belongs to all but finitely many members of V.
You should spell out that Ω denotes the family of all open ω-covers of X and Γ the family of all γ-covers of X.
If you mention the binomial notation, you should define it: (Ω choose Γ) means that every member of Ω contains a subfamily in Γ.
If you mention S1(Ω,Γ), you should define it explicitly as the one-element selection principle from a sequence of open ω-covers producing a γ-cover.
The paper records the easy direction (Ω choose Γ) ⇒ δ; the open content is the converse.
No extra set-theoretic hypothesis is part of Problem 5.1 itself; it is posed outright for sets of reals.
refined_question: Let X be a set of real numbers. For a sequence (A_n)_{n∈N} of subsets of X, define lim inf A_n = ⋃_{m∈N} ⋂_{n≥m} A_n, and for a family F of subsets of X let L(F) be the smallest family containing F and closed under this lim inf operation. Say that X has the δ-property if for every open ω-cover U of X, one has X ∈ L(U), where an open ω-cover is a family U of open subsets of X such that X ∉ U and every finite F ⊆ X is contained in some member of U. Is the δ-property equivalent to the Gerlits–Nagy γ-property, i.e. must every such X satisfy that every open ω-cover of X contains a γ-cover of X (equivalently, satisfy S1(Ω,Γ)), where a γ-cover is an infinite open cover in which each point of X belongs to all but finitely many members?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: if X is a set of real numbers with the δ-property and (U_n)_{n∈N} is a sequence of open ω-covers of X, must there exist U_n ∈ U_n for each n such that {U_n : n∈N} is a γ-cover of X?
justification: The draft is aiming at Section 5, Problem 5.1, not at a neighboring problem: Section 5 introduces lim inf, L(F), and the δ-property in exactly the way your draft does, and then asks whether the δ-property is equivalent to the property denoted by (Ω choose Γ). Section 1 supplies the missing notation and scope: the meanings of (A choose B), S1(A,B), ω-cover, and γ-cover, and the chapter’s restriction to sets of real numbers. The nearby Problem 5.2 is only auxiliary context: the paper notes that a negative answer there would imply a negative answer to Problem 5.1, but it is not the same question.
